Risk Scenario: If the LLM sub-processor uses Northstar data for model improvement, commercially sensitive demand and pricing information may be absorbed into a model serving other customers, with no route to recall it.
Proposed Treatment: Written opt-out from model improvement executed before any data transfer; contractual prohibition on training use; annual written confirmation.

Risk Scenario: If the vendor substitutes a sub-processor without Northstar approval, data may be processed by an entity that has never been assessed.
Proposed Treatment: Sub-processor list pinned in contract; substitution requires 60 days notice and Northstar written approval; right to terminate without penalty on objection.

Risk Scenario: If the AI inference component is compromised or misconfigured, Northstar data may be exposed through a pathway that no independent assurance covers.
Proposed Treatment: SOC 2 scope extended to include AI inference at next audit cycle; interim independent penetration test of the inference path at vendor cost.

Risk Scenario: If the vendor suffers a breach, Northstar may learn of it after its own regulatory notification window has begun to run.
Proposed Treatment: Contractual notification reduced to 24 hours from vendor awareness, with defined content requirements.

Risk Scenario: If personal data of Northstar customer contacts is processed without documented lawful basis, Northstar may be in breach of PIPEDA as controller.
Proposed Treatment: Executed DPA specifying Northstar as controller and vendor as processor; processing limited to documented instructions; no independent vendor use.

Risk Scenario: If vendor administrators hold standing access to the Northstar tenant, misuse or compromise of a vendor account may expose data without Northstar visibility.
Proposed Treatment: Just-in-time vendor access with Northstar approval; admin activity logs exposed to Northstar; quarterly review.

Risk Scenario: If the vendor fails or the relationship ends, Northstar may be unable to recover usable data or transition, because export is proprietary and untested.
Proposed Treatment: Tested export to open format before go-live; documented conversion path; deletion certificate on termination; exit plan reviewed annually.

Risk Scenario: If the vendor's 8-hour RTO applies during a peak ordering period, forecasting unavailability may disrupt order planning beyond Northstar's 4-hour tolerance.
Proposed Treatment: Documented manual fallback for demand planning; RTO commitment renegotiated to 4 hours at next renewal.

Risk Scenario: If the vendor is hosted in the same cloud region as Northstar's ERP and identity platform, a regional provider failure may remove multiple critical services simultaneously.
Proposed Treatment: Concentration recorded in the enterprise register against TPR-03; deployment region confirmed and monitored.

Risk Scenario: If liability is capped at 12 months of fees, Northstar may carry the majority of loss from a vendor-caused incident.
Proposed Treatment: Enhanced liability cap for data breach and confidentiality claims; vendor cyber insurance evidenced annually.
